title: A Cave in the Woods: Short Text Game
author: avoision
selftext:
I made this game using a mixture of my own writing, dynamic responses from AI (Claude), and whatever a user wishes to enter. Not sure how to best describe the "game" here - silly? Dark? A bit of both?

I had a lot of fun making this, and got significantly more experience learning how to work with AI on a coding project. As things progressed, I started to lean on AI to handle testing as well as the actual building of the game. 

  
Also found using the "Immaculate" skill to be helpful, in terms of suggestions and refinements.

On the testing front: I ended up having AI create new skills that were more or less customized E2E tests. I had just started to set up testing runs to kick off right before going to bed (so that I could utilize windows of time that would normally go unused). I'd wake up with a fresh report of issues to tackle. Also had a side skill that focused on chaos testing, in attempts to get the AI to drop a persona, break the game, etc.

  
Having AI keep an actual bug list (active/resolved/deferred) was also quite helpful.

  
More than anything else though, I had a lot of fun watching what the AI came up with, in its responses. More than once, the AI gave a response that made me genuinely laugh out loud. That was surprising, and made it really fun to develop. It got interesting, trying to figure out how to translate humor and what makes something funny, into a prompt for AI to use as a template.

  
Hope you get a laugh out of playing.
